title: France's cultural outings remain near pre-pandemic levels, but place, education, income, and mobility still sort access
source_unit: French Ministry of Culture, Baromètre des sorties culturelles 2025, DEPS and Crédoc
geography: France; residents aged 15 and above, France-wide

denominator.unit: France residents aged 15 and above surveyed in the Crédoc Conditions de vie et aspirations online survey

cinema_attendance.unit: percent attending cinema in the previous 12 months

live_show_attendance.unit: percent attending a professional live show in the previous 12 months

monument_visit.unit: percent visiting a monument in the previous 12 months

museum_exhibition_visit.unit: percent visiting a museum or exhibition in the previous 12 months

library_visit.unit: percent visiting a library or media library in the previous 12 months

festival_attendance.unit: percent attending a festival in the previous 12 months

mechanism.value: Physical cultural outings remain a routine mass activity, but participation is venue-specific: monuments and cinema reach much more of the population than museums, libraries, or festivals

observations.method: Annual cultural-outings barometer conducted with Crédoc within the Conditions de vie et aspirations survey; online fieldwork in January 2026 with retrospective questions on 2025 attendance.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates are self-reported annual recall measures and do not establish frequency-adjusted spending, causal recovery, or whether attendance was discretionary, educational, or work-related.
observations.subgroup: Residents of France aged 15 and above.
observations.counterinterpretation: Near-2019 rates can coexist with changed audience composition, prices, venue mix, or intensity; a one-year aggregate rate does not show individual continuity.

observations.period: 2025 reference year; demographic and place gradients

denominator.unit: France residents aged 15 and above surveyed in the Crédoc Conditions de vie et aspirations online survey

cinema_age_70_plus.unit: percent of ages 70 and above attending cinema

museum_bac_plus_3.unit: percent of people with three or more years of higher education visiting a museum or exhibition

museum_below_secondary.unit: percent of people with no diploma or lower secondary certification visiting a museum or exhibition

cinema_high_income.unit: percent of high-income respondents attending cinema

cinema_low_income.unit: percent of low-income respondents attending cinema

cinema_large_urban_centres.unit: percent of residents of large urban centres attending cinema

cinema_rural_dispersed.unit: percent of residents in dispersed rural areas attending cinema

mechanism.value: Cultural optionality is stratified by age, education, income, and settlement type: the same national attendance rate hides sharply unequal access to different cultural places

observations.method: Cross-tabulation from the barometer's 2025 attendance table by age, diploma, income class, and commune-density category.
observations.uncertainty: These are descriptive gradients, not causal effects of education, income, urbanity, or age; the online survey and subgroup definitions may affect comparability.
observations.subgroup: France residents aged 15 and above, disaggregated by age, education, income class, and settlement density.
observations.counterinterpretation: Urban and higher-education groups may differ simultaneously in transport, employment, household composition, school exposure, cultural supply, and reporting norms.

observations.period: 2025 reference year; cultural outings and tourism mobility

denominator.unit: France residents aged 15 and above surveyed in the Crédoc Conditions de vie et aspirations online survey

museum_visitors_with_overnight_stay.unit: percent of museum visitors associating the outing with a stay including at least one overnight

festival_goers_with_overnight_stay.unit: percent of festival attendees associating the outing with a stay including at least one overnight

fete_de_la_musique_participation.unit: percent participating in Fête de la musique

european_heritage_days_visit.unit: percent visiting as part of European Heritage Days

mechanism.value: Some cultural demand is a mobility bundle rather than a local venue visit: museums and festivals can generate overnight travel, while national events widen access through lower-threshold public programming

observations.method: Survey questions link museum and festival attendance to overnight stays and measure participation in two national cultural events; the report also identifies lack of availability, lack of interest, and fear of crowding as leading barriers.
observations.uncertainty: The overnight-stay measure is an association reported by visitors, not a causal tourism multiplier; the event participation measures do not identify spending, travel distance, or repeat attendance.
observations.subgroup: France residents aged 15 and above who attended museums or festivals, plus the full survey population for national events.
observations.counterinterpretation: A cultural outing may be incidental to a trip rather than its purpose, and national events may attract different publics because of timing, free access, or local programming.

related_sources.claim: French Ministry of Culture publication page provides the release date, headline results, scope, and survey partnership.
Official 24-page barometer contains attendance trends, demographic and settlement gradients, cultural-tourism mobility, event participation, and barriers.

boundary: This record adds French evidence on physical cultural attendance, socioeconomic and settlement stratification, cultural-tourism mobility, and barriers. It is a commissioned online self-report survey and does not establish causal recovery, actual spending, venue supply effects, or individual-level cultural trajectories.
